_note: Planning-level estimates for an SRR. Every value marked 'assumption' is ours and should be refined; 'sourced' values cite sources.json. Staff salaries are deliberately excluded (set aside by the team).

capex_items.name: 30 m self-supporting lattice tower, foundation, grounding and lightning protection
Voice loudspeaker array, 3.2 kW class (about 124 dBC at 100 ft, about 1.28 km to 70 dB)
capex_items.basis: assumption; performance class from Federal Signal Modulator spec, tone-siren list price reference $17,387 (Darley Sentry 15)

capex_items.name: Solar PV 6 kWp + 40 kWh LiFePO4 storage + controller
Hand-crank generator (manual backup for radios and alert playback)
S-3 fixed responder terminal and antenna (S3-08 class)
Commercial broadband backhaul kit (Starlink Standard, optional)
Prefab station building, about 60 m2 (ops room, storage, bunks)
Medical cache, water purification, sensor spares and charging, A-2 drone landing pad interface

remote.name: Boat or motorbikes, plus airlift interface (A-3)

logistics_multiplier._basis: assumption: cost to haul materials and build at the site

hydro_option.name: 3 kW micro-hydro (run-of-river) replacing most of the solar/battery bank
hydro_option._basis: assumption at about $5,000/kW for micro scale. For scale reference, DRC's 13.8 MW Matebe run-of-river plant cost about $19.7M (about $1,430/kW); micro plants cost several times more per kW.

community_receiver._basis: assumption: one receiver per village (about 500 people) and one per 5,000 urban residents at public points (schools, markets, churches)

loudspeaker._basis: 1.28 km = 4,200 ft range to 70 dB for a 3.2 kW array (Federal Signal spec). Clustering factor: rural people live in villages along roads/rivers, so local density near a station is several times the cell average (assumption).

radio._basis: assumption: VHF from a 30 m tower to handhelds in forest terrain

budget.basis: RFP S-3 life-cycle cost cap over 15 years incl. replenishment (TBR)
